title: In Support of Longer, Healthier Lives For Australia’s Men
author: Aaron
body:
The clock is ticking. Every hour in Australia, at least four men die from preventable diseases, leaving a devasting impact on the lives of their families and the wider community.

At every stage of life, the rates of mortality for cancer, diabetes and diseases of the circulatory system are higher for men than for women. We see their effects compounded with 74 per cent of alcohol-related deaths also occurring in men, while more than two-thirds of Australian men are overweight or obese. A large number also experience depression at some point in their life. As with all health-related issues, awareness and early diagnosis are key.

The importance of addressing these issues resonated with the committee, and OneTomorrow recently had the pleasure of hearing from Professor Gary Richardson, who sits on the board of Foundation 49: Men’s Health. Created in honour of the late journalist Tony Hitchin, the foundation’s vision is to enable men to live longer and healthier lives. A respected oncologist, Professor Richardson spoke about how modern scientific and medical research is making it easier than ever before for men to become informed about their specific health concerns.

By focusing on conditions that may occur during each stage of life, Foundation 49 educates men on the causes, as well as respective prevention and treatment options. Key risk factors for men can include drinking too much alcohol, falling prey to depression and self-harm while in their twenties, and becoming too sedentary in their later years.

A major component of the foundation’s work also involves helping men to take an active interest in their reproductive and sexual health. It achieves this through providing evidence-based information that is inclusive of everyone, regardless of education, religion or ethnicity.

As part of his presentation, Professor Richardson explained how everyone has a stake in the improvement of men’s health. Partners, families, employers and the wider community benefit from an overall increase in men’s health status.

Recognising the importance of supporting a cause that represents 49 per cent of the community, OneTomorrow reached out to Professor Richardson and Foundation 49 to contribute a $2,000 donation. These funds will further enable the valuable not-for-profit to continue its work promoting health and wellbeing to men of all ages.
